title: Invitation to a Service Review
prompt: Good morning, everyone. Our customer service team will hold a short review on Thursday at two o'clock. We will discuss last week's delayed responses and identify ways to improve our support process. Please bring one example of a difficult request and one suggestion for handling it more efficiently. The meeting will take place in the conference room on the third floor.
sample_answer: Good morning, everyone. / Our customer service team will hold a short review / on Thursday at two o'clock. / We will discuss last week's delayed responses / and identify ways to improve our support process. / Please bring one example of a difficult request / and one suggestion for handling it more efficiently. / The meeting will take place / in the conference room on the third floor.
tips_md:
**Luyện đọc lời mời họp:**
- Ngắt hơi sau lời chào và từng cụm thông tin về thời gian, mục đích, việc cần chuẩn bị.
- Nhấn **Thursday**, **two o'clock**, **one example** và **one suggestion** để người nghe nắm yêu cầu.
- Luyện phụ âm cuối của **requests**, **responses**, **floor**; giữ nhịp đều khi đọc cụm dài **handling it more efficiently**.
- Dùng giọng lịch sự cho câu bắt đầu bằng **Please bring** và hạ giọng khi kết thúc thông báo.

title: New Office Visitor Procedure
prompt: Welcome to Northpoint Offices. All visitors must sign in at the reception desk before entering the work areas. Please show a photo identification card and tell our receptionist whom you are meeting. You will receive a temporary badge, which must remain visible during your visit. Before leaving, return the badge to reception. Thank you for helping us keep the building secure.
sample_answer: Welcome to Northpoint Offices. / All visitors must sign in / at the reception desk / before entering the work areas. / Please show a photo identification card / and tell our receptionist whom you are meeting. / You will receive a temporary badge, / which must remain visible during your visit. / Before leaving, / return the badge to reception. / Thank you for helping us keep the building secure.
tips_md:
**Thông báo quy trình đón khách:**
- Nhóm ý theo thứ tự **sign in → show identification → wear a badge → return the badge**.
- Đánh dấu chỗ lấy hơi trước **which must remain visible** để mệnh đề quan hệ không bị đứt đoạn.
- Phát âm rõ **visitors**, **temporary**, **receptionist**, đặc biệt âm /s/ cuối của **Offices**.
- Khi đọc hướng dẫn an ninh, giữ giọng rõ và thân thiện thay vì nhấn quá mạnh từ **must**.

title: Product Research Invitation
prompt: Have you used our new expense tracking application? We are inviting volunteers to take part in a thirty-minute interview next Wednesday. During the session, you will try a few common tasks and tell us what feels easy or confusing. No technical knowledge is required. Participants will receive a small thank-you gift. To register, contact the product research team by Monday afternoon.
sample_answer: Have you used our new expense tracking application? / We are inviting volunteers / to take part in a thirty-minute interview / next Wednesday. / During the session, / you will try a few common tasks / and tell us what feels easy or confusing. / No technical knowledge is required. / Participants will receive a small thank-you gift. / To register, / contact the product research team / by Monday afternoon.
tips_md:
**Đọc lời mời nghiên cứu người dùng:**
- Lên giọng nhẹ ở câu hỏi đầu, sau đó chuyển sang giọng thông báo.
- Nhấn **thirty-minute interview**, **next Wednesday** và **Monday afternoon** để phân biệt ngày tham gia và hạn đăng ký.
- Luyện nhịp từ dài **application**, **participants**, **technical**; tránh nuốt âm ở **tasks**.
- Dừng ngắn trước **No technical knowledge is required** để làm nổi bật thông tin trấn an người nghe.

title: A New Invoice Dashboard
prompt: Dear business customers, we have introduced a new online dashboard for tracking invoices. You can now view payment dates, download monthly statements, and report billing questions from one page. Existing account details will remain the same. If you need assistance, our finance support team is available from nine in the morning until five in the afternoon on weekdays. We appreciate your feedback.

tips_md:
**Thông báo tính năng tài chính:**
- Đọc danh sách ba chức năng với cùng nhịp: **view**, **download**, **report**.
- Nhấn cặp thời gian **nine** và **five** và đọc rõ **on weekdays** để tránh gây hiểu sai giờ hỗ trợ.
- Tách hai cụm **existing account details** và **will remain the same** để làm rõ nội dung bảo đảm.
- Luyện âm cuối trong **dates**, **statements** và trọng âm từ **assistance**.

prompt: This is a reminder for employees who have borrowed equipment from the IT department. Our staff will check the equipment and provide a confirmation email. The collection desk is open every afternoon except Friday.

- Giảm tốc ở câu có hạn trả để tránh người nghe nhầm thời hạn.

- Nhấn **Tuesday morning** là thời gian học, **Friday** là hạn đăng ký.
- Lấy hơi ở cuối câu **Please bring a laptop and a pair of headphones** để câu yêu cầu nghe tự nhiên.

title: Interview: Daily Team Updates
prompt:
A workplace research team is asking employees about short daily meetings.
Question 1: How does your team usually share updates at the beginning of the day?
Question 2: What makes a daily update meeting useful for you?
Question 3: What would you change if your team's daily meetings were taking too long?
sample_answer:
Q1: We usually have a ten-minute video call where everyone mentions their main task for the day.
Q2: I find it useful when people explain what is blocking their work. Someone else can often help right away.
Q3: If our meetings became too long, I would ask everyone to prepare one short update in advance. We could discuss detailed technical issues separately with the people involved. That would keep the main meeting focused and give everyone more time to work.
tips_md:
**Khảo sát về họp đầu ngày:**
- Câu 1 nêu kênh trao đổi và thời lượng bằng một câu ngắn.
- Câu 2 dùng **blocking their work** để nói về trở ngại mà đồng đội có thể hỗ trợ.
- Câu 3 đưa hai giải pháp cụ thể **prepare updates** và **discuss details separately**.
- Phân bổ 15–15–30 giây; ghi âm kiểm tra phần trả lời cuối có giải pháp và kết quả.

title: Interview: Reporting Software Problems
prompt:
A software quality team wants to understand how people report problems with digital products.
Question 1: What do you normally do first when an application stops working?
Question 2: Have you ever sent a bug report to a product team?
Question 3: What information should a clear bug report include, and why?
sample_answer:
Q1: I usually check my connection and try the action once more to see whether the problem happens again.
Q2: Yes, I reported an issue with a calendar app because an event disappeared after I saved it.
Q3: A useful report should explain what the user was trying to do, the steps that caused the problem, and what actually happened. A screenshot and the app version can also help. These details make it easier for developers to reproduce the issue and find a fix.
tips_md:
**Khảo sát về báo lỗi:**
- Câu 1 trả lời bằng thao tác đầu tiên, không lan sang cách sửa toàn bộ sự cố.
- Câu 2 dùng một ví dụ đời thường có hành động và hiện tượng rõ ràng.
- Câu 3 phân biệt **steps**, **expected result**, **actual result** khi luyện mở rộng bài nói.
- Phát âm rõ **reproduce**, **screenshot**, **version**; dành nửa thời gian cho câu 3.

title: Survey: Effective Online Meetings
prompt:
A human resources team is collecting feedback about online meetings.
Question 1: Which device do you usually use to join an online meeting?
Question 2: What do you do when you cannot hear another speaker clearly?
Question 3: What two habits would help remote meetings run more smoothly?
sample_answer:
Q1: I usually join from my laptop because it is easier to view shared documents.
Q2: I politely ask the person to repeat the last point, and I check my audio settings if the problem continues.
Q3: First, I think everyone should read the agenda before joining, so we can start with the important decisions. Second, participants should mute their microphones when they are not speaking. This reduces background noise. A short summary at the end would also help everyone remember the next steps.
tips_md:
**Khảo sát về họp trực tuyến:**
- Câu 1 nêu thiết bị và một lý do thực tế.
- Câu 2 luyện câu lịch sự **Could you repeat the last point, please?**.
- Câu 3 đưa hai thói quen và giải thích tác dụng của từng thói quen, tránh chỉ liệt kê.
- Thực hành ngữ điệu lịch sự ở **politely ask** và giữ câu trả lời cuối trong 30 giây.

title: Interview: Writing Work Instructions
prompt:
A company is reviewing how staff members create and use internal instructions.
Question 1: When do you usually look for written instructions at work?
Question 2: What kind of instructions do you find easiest to follow?
Question 3: How could your team keep shared documentation accurate over time?
sample_answer:
Q1: I usually read instructions when I need to use a tool that I have not worked with before.
Q2: I prefer short steps with screenshots because I can follow them while doing the task.
Q3: My team could assign one person to review each important document every few months. We could also add a feedback button so employees can flag outdated steps. Whenever a process changes, the person making the change should update the document. That would make the information more reliable for new colleagues.
tips_md:
**Trao đổi về tài liệu nội bộ:**
- Phân biệt **when** ở câu 1 và **what kind** ở câu 2 để tránh trả lời lạc đề.
- Tận dụng từ vựng **step-by-step instructions**, **screenshots**, **outdated**.
- Câu 3 có thể triển khai vòng lặp **review → report outdated steps → update**.
- Nêu trách nhiệm cụ thể của người cập nhật tài liệu để đề xuất thuyết phục.

title: Interview: Welcoming New Clients
prompt:
A business services company is interviewing employees about the client onboarding experience.
Question 1: What is the first thing you would explain to a new client?
Question 2: Which communication method would you use for a quick follow-up?
Question 3: How would you help a client who feels overwhelmed by a new software platform?
sample_answer:
Q1: I would explain where clients can find their main account information and how to contact support.
Q2: For a quick update, I would send a short email with a clear subject line.
Q3: I would start by asking which task the client needs to complete first. Then I would demonstrate that one task slowly and let them try it. I could send a simple checklist afterward and arrange another call if they still had questions. Small steps would help the client feel more confident.
tips_md:
**Giao tiếp với khách hàng mới:**
- Câu 1 ưu tiên thông tin thiết yếu, tránh giới thiệu mọi tính năng.
- Câu 2 nêu phương tiện và đặc điểm của thông điệp, chẳng hạn **a short email**.
- Câu 3 dùng cấu trúc **ask → demonstrate → let them try → follow up** để thể hiện sự hỗ trợ từng bước.
- Luyện từ **overwhelmed** và ngữ điệu kiên nhẫn, thân thiện.

title: Survey: Using Data Dashboards
prompt:
An operations manager is asking employees about visual reports.
Question 1: How often do you look at performance charts at work or school?
Question 2: Which is easier for you to understand, a simple chart or a long table?
Question 3: What should a dashboard designer do to help users find important information quickly?
sample_answer:
Q1: I check a small performance dashboard every Monday before our planning meeting.
Q2: I find a simple chart easier to understand when I want to see changes over time.
Q3: I think the designer should put the most important numbers near the top and use clear labels for every chart. There should also be an option to filter information by date. For example, a sales manager might need to compare this week with the previous week. A clean layout would make that comparison much faster.
tips_md:
**Khảo sát về biểu đồ dữ liệu:**
- Câu 1 cho biết tần suất cụ thể như **every Monday**.
- Câu 2 chọn một cách trình bày và nói rõ tình huống sử dụng.
- Câu 3 dùng ví dụ so sánh theo thời gian để chứng minh tác dụng của **filters** và **clear labels**.
- Tập phân biệt phát âm **chart**, **dashboard**, **compare**.

title: Interview: Making Websites Easier to Use
prompt:
A web design group wants feedback on features that make websites easier for different users.
Question 1: What makes a website easy for you to navigate?
Question 2: Have you ever struggled to read text on a website?
Question 3: Which accessibility improvements should a small business prioritize on its website?
sample_answer:
Q1: Clear menus and descriptive buttons help me find what I need quickly.
Q2: Yes, I once visited a website that used very pale text on a white background, and it was difficult to read.
Q3: I would start with readable text and strong color contrast. I would also make sure that visitors can use the menus with a keyboard. For example, someone who cannot use a mouse should still be able to complete a booking form. These changes would help more customers use the service independently.
tips_md:
**Trả lời về khả năng truy cập website:**
- Câu 1 nêu yếu tố điều hướng, câu 2 nêu trải nghiệm đọc chữ.
- Câu 3 chọn hai ưu tiên có thể kiểm tra được **contrast** và **keyboard navigation**.
- Sử dụng tình huống điền biểu mẫu để làm rõ lợi ích thực tế.
- Tránh nói chung chung **make it better**; dùng động từ **read**, **navigate**, **complete**.

title: Interview: Managing Unexpected Delays
prompt:
A project management trainer is asking about how teams deal with schedule changes.
Question 1: How do you usually keep track of your own deadlines?
Question 2: Who would you contact first if you realized a task might be late?
Question 3: What would you say to a teammate whose work is delayed and who needs your help?
sample_answer:
Q1: I keep my deadlines in a task list and review it at the start of each day.
Q2: I would contact the project lead as soon as I noticed the risk.
Q3: I would ask my teammate what is causing the delay and which part I could help with. If the problem is technical, we could spend twenty minutes looking at it together. I would also suggest updating the team on the new timeline. That way, we could solve the immediate problem and manage expectations.
tips_md:
**Giao tiếp khi công việc trễ hạn:**
- Câu 1 trả lời cách theo dõi cá nhân, tránh kể quá nhiều ứng dụng.
- Câu 2 nhấn **as soon as I noticed the risk** để thể hiện chủ động.
- Câu 3 dùng câu hỏi hỗ trợ **What part can I help with?** và đề cập cập nhật lịch.
- Luyện nói với thái độ hợp tác, tránh các câu đổ lỗi cho đồng nghiệp.

title: Survey: Learning Technical Skills at Work
prompt:
A training coordinator is surveying employees about job-related technology skills.
Question 1: Which digital skill have you used most often this month?
Question 2: How do you usually practice a skill after attending a training session?
Question 3: What could employers do to make technical training more useful in daily work?
sample_answer:
Q1: I have used spreadsheet formulas almost every day to prepare simple reports.
Q2: I usually practice with a small task from my actual job so I can remember the steps.
Q3: Employers could give staff a short practice project after each workshop. They could also provide a place where employees can ask follow-up questions. For example, after learning a new reporting tool, people could build one real team report. This would show whether the training was useful and help them apply it immediately.
tips_md:
**Khảo sát về kỹ năng công nghệ:**
- Câu 1 gọi tên một kỹ năng cụ thể, chẳng hạn **spreadsheet formulas**.
- Câu 2 nói rõ cách thực hành sau đào tạo.
- Câu 3 kết hợp **a small practice project** với **follow-up questions** và một ví dụ liên quan công việc.
- Giữ ví dụ ngắn để đủ thời gian nói kết quả trong 30 giây cuối.

title: Releasing Software Features Gradually
prompt: Some software teams release new features to a small group of users before making them available to everyone. Do you think this is a good approach? Explain your opinion with reasons and an example.
sample_answer: I think releasing a feature to a small group first is a smart approach. One reason is that the team can discover problems before many people are affected. Another reason is that early users can explain which parts are confusing. For example, a shopping app could offer a new checkout screen to a few volunteers. If they have difficulty finding the payment button, the designers can improve it before the wider release. Of course, the company should tell participants that they are testing a new experience. Overall, a gradual release gives teams more useful feedback and reduces the risk of a frustrating launch.
tips_md:
**Nêu quan điểm về phát hành tính năng:**
- Chốt ý kiến ngay đầu bằng **a smart approach**, rồi đưa hai lý do riêng về rủi ro và phản hồi.
- Ví dụ cần có **new feature → small group → observed problem → improvement**.
- Nếu dùng từ **gradual release**, giải thích bằng ngôn ngữ dễ hiểu thay vì thuật ngữ kỹ thuật dài.
- Dành khoảng 10 giây mở bài, 40 giây lập luận và ví dụ, 10 giây kết luận.

title: Writing Down Decisions After Meetings
prompt: Should project teams send a short written summary of decisions after every important meeting? Give reasons and a specific example to support your answer.
sample_answer: Yes, I believe project teams should send short meeting summaries. First, people sometimes remember conversations differently, especially when a meeting includes many decisions. A written summary gives everyone one clear reference. Second, it helps colleagues who could not attend. For example, after a product planning meeting, the organizer could send three decisions, the person responsible for each task, and the deadline. Everyone would know what to do without asking the same questions again. The summary does not have to be long. A few clear bullet points are enough. In my experience, this small habit can prevent confusion and save time later.
tips_md:
**Lập luận về biên bản họp:**
- Trả lời thẳng **Yes** rồi giải thích hai lợi ích: thống nhất cách hiểu và cập nhật cho người vắng mặt.
- Ví dụ dùng cấu trúc **decision, owner, deadline** để cho thấy bản tóm tắt hữu ích ra sao.
- Nhấn mạnh **short written summary** để bám yêu cầu đề.
- Luyện chuyển ý bằng **First**, **Second**, **For example**, **In my experience**.

title: Accessibility Checks Before Launch
prompt: Do you think every company website should be checked for accessibility before it is launched, even when the team has a limited budget? Support your view with reasons and examples.
sample_answer: I think basic accessibility checks should be part of every website launch. Many customers use a keyboard or need text that is easy to read, so a website should work for different people. These checks can also reveal problems that affect everyone, such as confusing buttons or missing form labels. For example, a small restaurant could test whether customers can read its menu clearly and complete an online reservation without a mouse. The team may not have a large budget, but it can begin with simple checks and improve the site over time. That seems more responsible than waiting for customers to complain.
tips_md:
**Tranh luận về kiểm tra khả năng truy cập:**
- Công nhận điều kiện **limited budget** rồi đề xuất **basic checks** khả thi.
- Đưa hai lợi ích gắn với trải nghiệm sử dụng, không nêu khẳng định pháp lý khi đề không yêu cầu.
- Ví dụ gồm hai việc kiểm tra có thể quan sát: đọc menu và đặt bàn bằng bàn phím.
- Kết bằng kế hoạch cải tiến dần để lập luận thực tế.

title: Showing Rough Prototypes to Clients
prompt: Some designers show clients simple unfinished prototypes early in a project. Others wait until the design looks polished. Which approach do you prefer, and why?
sample_answer: I prefer showing a simple prototype early. It allows clients to explain what they actually need before the team spends too much time on details. It also makes discussions more specific because people can react to a screen instead of imagining a description. For instance, when designing a booking page, I would first show a basic layout with the date picker and confirmation button. The client might notice that customers need an option to change their appointment. We could add that feature before working on colors and images. I would clearly explain that the prototype is unfinished. Early feedback usually makes the final design more useful.
tips_md:
**So sánh cách giới thiệu bản mẫu:**
- Chọn **showing a prototype early** hoặc phương án còn lại và giữ lập trường xuyên suốt.
- Tách lý do về tiết kiệm công sửa và làm rõ yêu cầu khách hàng.
- Dùng ví dụ màn hình đặt lịch để minh họa phản hồi dẫn đến thay đổi cụ thể.
- Tránh mô tả bản mẫu như sản phẩm đã hoàn thiện; dùng **unfinished** và **early feedback**.

title: Setting Aside Time for Software Maintenance
prompt: Should development teams reserve part of each week for fixing small problems and improving existing features, even when there are requests for new features? Explain your reasons.
sample_answer: Yes, I think teams should reserve regular time for maintenance. Small problems may seem unimportant at first, but they can become frustrating when customers face them every day. Maintenance also helps developers understand and simplify older parts of the product. For example, a team might spend Friday morning fixing a slow search page and updating confusing error messages. Those changes could make the application easier to use without introducing a major new feature. The team still needs to deliver new ideas, so I would agree on a reasonable amount of maintenance time with the product manager. A balanced schedule can support both reliability and progress.
tips_md:
**Quan điểm về thời gian bảo trì:**
- Tập trung vào việc **reserve part of each week** như đề hỏi.
- Giải thích hai lợi ích riêng: trải nghiệm người dùng và chất lượng mã hiện có.
- Ví dụ nên có hai lỗi nhỏ cụ thể và tác động sau khi sửa.
- Kết luận nhấn sự cân bằng lịch phát triển, tránh nêu tỷ lệ phần trăm tùy tiện.

title: Sharing Project Progress with Clients
prompt: Do you think clients should be able to view a simple project progress dashboard throughout a service project? Give reasons and examples for your opinion.
sample_answer: I think a simple progress dashboard is helpful for clients. It allows them to see what has been completed and what is coming next without sending frequent emails. It can also build trust because delays and changes are easier to discuss early. For example, during a website project, the dashboard could show whether the design, content review, and testing stages are complete. If testing takes an extra day, the project manager could update the expected date and explain the reason. The dashboard should use plain language and show only information the client needs. That would make communication clearer for both sides.
tips_md:
**Bày tỏ ý kiến về cập nhật tiến độ:**
- Hai luận điểm rõ là **fewer status emails** và **early discussion of changes**.
- Ví dụ cần có các giai đoạn dự án và cách thông báo khi chậm lịch.
- Ưu tiên từ dễ hiểu **completed**, **coming next**, **expected date** thay vì thuật ngữ quản lý phức tạp.
- Nói rõ giới hạn **simple** để bám sát câu hỏi và tính thực tế.

title: Reviewing Code with a Colleague
prompt: Some programming teams ask another developer to review changes before they are added to the main application. Do you think this practice is worth the extra time? Why or why not?
sample_answer: Yes, I think peer code review is worth the time. Another developer may notice a mistake or an unclear part of the code that the author has missed. Reviews also help teammates learn different ways to solve problems. For example, someone reviewing a new login form might notice that an error message is confusing or that an unusual input has not been considered. Fixing it before release could save much more time later. Reviews should be respectful and focused on the code rather than the person who wrote it. When teams keep feedback specific and useful, the process improves both quality and cooperation.
tips_md:
**Tranh luận về kiểm tra mã nguồn:**
- Đưa hai lợi ích **catch mistakes** và **share knowledge**.
- Ví dụ về biểu mẫu đăng nhập nên nhấn phát hiện lỗi và sửa trước khi phát hành.
- Dùng từ **specific feedback** để mô tả cách góp ý hiệu quả.
- Tập phát âm **review**, **developer**, **unusual input** và tránh nói quá nhanh ở ví dụ.

title: Automating Repetitive Office Tasks
prompt: Do you agree that companies should invest time in automating routine office tasks, such as copying information between reports, even if setting up the automation takes several days? Explain your answer.
sample_answer: I agree that automation is useful when a task is repeated often. Employees can spend less time copying information and more time checking results or helping customers. Automation may also reduce mistakes caused by entering the same data several times. For example, a small service company could connect its appointment list to a weekly report. Setting up that process might take a few days, but it could save time every Friday. I would still have someone review the output, especially when important customer information is involved. If the team chooses a stable process and checks the results, automation can be a worthwhile investment.
tips_md:
**Lập luận về tự động hóa công việc:**
- Nhấn điều kiện **repeated often** để giải thích vì sao đáng đầu tư thời gian ban đầu.
- Hai lợi ích riêng là tiết kiệm thao tác và giảm sai sót nhập liệu.
- Ví dụ cần có công việc trước khi tự động hóa, việc thiết lập và kết quả lặp lại hàng tuần.
- Thêm một câu về kiểm tra kết quả để thể hiện cách triển khai thực tế.

title: Sharing Solutions Across Teams
prompt: Should companies encourage employees to share short explanations of problems they have solved so that other teams can learn from them? Support your opinion with reasons and a real or imagined example.
sample_answer: I think sharing short explanations of solved problems is a great habit. It saves time because employees do not need to investigate the same issue again. It also helps newer team members learn how experienced colleagues make decisions. For example, a support specialist could write a short note explaining why customers sometimes receive duplicate notifications and how the team resolved the problem. If another department sees the same issue, the note could guide its first steps. The explanation should include the cause, the solution, and when to ask for more help. A small library of practical notes could make the whole company more effective.
tips_md:
**Nêu quan điểm về chia sẻ kinh nghiệm:**
- Mở bằng **I think sharing...** để thể hiện lập trường rõ ràng.
- Phát triển hai lý do: tránh điều tra trùng lặp và hỗ trợ nhân viên mới.
- Ví dụ nên trình bày theo **problem → cause → solution → reuse**.
- Kết bằng lợi ích dài hạn của một thư viện hướng dẫn ngắn, tránh lặp nguyên văn luận điểm đầu.
